title: Endpoint latency exposure map — p95/p99 rollups and regression watchlists by route, model, region
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
Build a single-pane "latency exposure map" that surfaces p95 and p99 latency rollups across the three primary dimensions we use for routing and capacity planning: route (API path), model (model name + quantization/variant), and region (cloud region / availability zone). The map will support drill-downs to token/sec, batch-size distribution, KV-cache hit-rate slices, and historical regression watchlists so SRE/Platform can quickly triage degradations and plan mitigation (e.g., scale, fallback to cheaper variant).

Why this is needed:
- Current dashboards show percentile signals, but it's hard to answer: "Which route+model+region combinations are becoming expensive or risky?"
- Engineers spend time assembling ad-hoc queries during incidents. We want a canonical explorer and alerting surface to reduce MTTI and improve runbooks.

Goals / success metrics:
- Interactive exposure map that can display p95 and p99 as heatmaps and sortable rollups across route/model/region in <2s for common queries.
- Regression watchlists that detect >10% relative increase in p95 or absolute increase >50ms sustained for 15 minutes with configurable sensitivity.
- Dashboards and drill paths for triage: top 20 worst combos by p99, distributions of tokens/sec and batch size, KV cache hit-rate overlay.
- Reduce time-to-identify primary dimension (route/model/region) for latency incidents by 50% in first 90 days.

Progress so far:
- Telemetry spec drafted and reviewed with ingest team (link below). We agreed on a compact tag set to avoid cardinality explosion: route, model_name, model_variant, region, hw_tier, batch_size_bucket, kv_cache_hit (true/false), tokens_generated_bucket.
- Prototype queries in ClickHouse that compute per-slice p95/p99 rollups and retention-friendly downsampled rollups (1m/5m). Proof-of-concept dashboard created in Grafana.
- Regression detection prototype using EWMA + Bayesian change-point on recent 1h window; initial results flagged historical regressions from last 2 months in our playback corpus.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Cardinality cap: we will cap labels to route+model_variant+region and collapse uncommon batch_size buckets into "other" to keep shards small. This sacrifices granularity for stability.
- Storage: two-tier rollups — high-resolution (1m) for 30 days, aggregated (5m) for 90 days. This is a trade between query latency and cost.
- Detection policy: default sensitivity for platform teams, with per-customer stricter thresholds (configurable in Console).

Artifacts / links:
- Telemetry spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/latency-exposure-map-telemetry-spec
- Grafana prototype dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency-exposure-map/proto-99123
- ClickHouse query set & materialized views: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-monitoring/pull/412
- Regression algorithm notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_the-notebook
- Incident playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Playbook+-+latency-exposure-map

Reviewer feedback (summary):
- PM (Rina Torres): prefer faster default rollups; asked for export of watchlist to Slack and Console.
- Observability lead (Samir Patel): asked to limit additional tags and validate cardinality via a synthetic run.
- SRE (Lena Morales): requested a 2-minute emergency short-circuit alert pathway to notify canary and fallback engineers.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Finalize telemetry emitter changes in runtime (tags + batch_size bucketing) — blocker: runtime change in runtime-1.22 branch.
2) Create ClickHouse materialized views for p95/p99 per slice and downsampled rollups.
3) Build Grafana panel set + exposure map UI (table + heatmap) and wire drilldowns to pre-defined queries.
4) Implement regression watcher service that evaluates slices each minute and writes alerts into the watchlist index.
5) Console integration: expose watchlist, enable per-team thresholds and Slack/Email integration.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Telemetry changes deployed to staging and validated with synthetic harness (no >10% cardinality growth).
- [ ] Materialized views populated in staging; queries return p95/p99 rollups for 99% of slices in <2s.
- [ ] Grafana dashboard has heatmap + drilldown links; product review signoff obtained.
- [ ] Regression watcher can detect and surface historical regressions in playback within expected sensitivity; alerts route to watchlist and Slack.
- [ ] Runbook and playbook updated and linked from dashboard.

Playbook notes (short):
- On a watchlist alert: open the heatmap, filter by the slice, check batch_size and tokens/sec distribution for sudden shifts, check KV-cache hit rate. If traffic pattern change suspected, trigger a canary scale or model fallback. If model regression suspected, follow model-rollout rollback playbook.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finish telemetry emitter PR and schedule runtime-1.22 deploy to staging (owner: Jonah Park).
- Run synthetic playback across top 200 routes to validate cardinality and signal quality (owner: QA observability).
- Iterate on Grafana prototype per PM feedback, add Console watchlist export.

Notes for reviewers: please check the telemetry tag list and the cardinality guardrails first. If you have historical slices you want prioritized in the watchlist please add them in comments below or in the Confluence page.
